label.en: Transport and logistics — carrier, broker or warehousing
label.fr: Transport et logistique — transporteur, courtier ou entreposage

notes:
SCOPE HONESTY — READ THIS BEFORE THE FIRST MEETING. We have NO TRANSPORT-MANAGEMENT CAPABILITY. There is no load board, no dispatch board, no route optimization, no rating engine with accessorial or fuel-surcharge tables, no driver or owner-operator settlement engine, and no fuel-tax (IFTA) reporting. A carrier or a broker therefore needs a dedicated transport-management system with our ERP sitting behind it as finance — Trimble, Axon, TruckMate, Shipwell and similar are the systems these clients already shop. SAY THIS IN THE FIRST MEETING, not in the proposal. Selling an ERP as a replacement for dispatch and settlement in this sector is how a consultancy loses a reference. ind_transport.sys.q01 exists specifically to establish which of those pieces the client already has, because that answer, not our module list, defines the engagement.

WHERE WE DO FIT, and what the audit should be aimed at: third-party warehousing and logistics billing (storage, handling, in and out), freight cost allocation into landed cost, fleet and equipment maintenance cost, procurement, and the whole finance and reporting layer above whatever runs dispatch. The realistic engagement is integration plus operational reporting — load-level profitability, cost per kilometre, settlement accuracy, receivables — not replacement of the operating system.

BENCHMARKS: NONE. Our transport benchmark figures (on-time delivery 88.5 percent average, empty kilometres 22 percent average and 12 percent top quartile, order cycle time 3.2 days, claims ratio 1.8 percent, operating ratio below 0.95, spot rates per mile) all trace to a single aggregator source and the transport benchmark literature is thin. They are CONVERSATION ANCHORS the consultant may use verbally; they are NOT defensible in a written report and NO benchmark_ref is set anywhere in this bank. Every numeric question here says in its help text that we use the client's own number. If a client's controller asks where a figure came from and the answer is an aggregator blog, we have lost the room.

QUEBEC: ind_transport.comp.q02 asks whether any part of the business is paid passenger transport, which is one of the two sectors subject to Revenu Quebec's facturation obligatoire regime and requires a separately certified sales-recording system that we are not. Ask the question only. DO NOT state dates, generations or deadlines — our research on those is not from a primary Revenu Quebec page. The consultant verifies against Revenu Quebec and its published certified-product list before anything goes in writing.

REVEALS KEYS INTRODUCED BY THIS BANK (cost-model inputs; must exist in scoring/scoring.v1.json#cost_model.inputs before this bank goes live):
- accessorials_uncaptured_rate — share of earned accessorials (detention, waiting time, lumper, redelivery, layover) that never reach an invoice. The single largest revenue leak in this sector and the headline dollar figure.
- pod_to_invoice_days — working days from proof of delivery to invoice issued. Feeds the working-capital module, which is gated on base.fin.q07 (line of credit drawn).
- empty_km_pct — percentage of kilometres run empty. Feeds the fuel and equipment cost module.
- settlement_hours_per_cycle — hours per settlement cycle spent calculating driver and owner-operator pay. Feeds the labour saving.
- claims_cost_annual — CAD of claims absorbed in the last 12 months, including amounts offset against customer invoices.
- cost_per_km_known — boolean: whether the client can state a loaded-kilometre cost and name what is inside it. Gates the load-profitability module; without it we cannot monetize anything load-level and must say so.

questions.notes: ODOO GAP. There is no rating engine: no lane-based rate tables, no accessorial schedules, no minimum charges, no tariff rounding, no class or weight-break logic. questions.notes: ODOO GAP, and a people risk at the same time. There is no settlement engine — no per-kilometre or percentage pay models, no stop pay, no detention split, no advance or déduction ledger. Settlement in a chiffrier maintained by one person is simultaneously the client's biggest single-point-of-failure and the reason driver disputes never get resolved cleanly. Record who that person is by name in the report.
